title: Four Levers
tagline: No hydraulics in a C-5: steer with four thrust levers.
history: Inspired by airliners that lost every flight control to hydraulic failures — a 1989 wide-body above all, whose crew steered it to a runway with the throttles alone, saving most of those aboard — and the research into thrust-only control that followed.
situation: Fifteen miles east of Brize Norton at 5,000 ft, a heavy C-5 with 40 aboard loses every hydraulic system. Nothing moves when you move the yoke — but there are four engines, two on each wing.
failures: Hydraulic systems green, blue and yellow lost: all flight controls frozen
No flaps, no speed brakes; gear by gravity; brakes on the accumulator
tips: Split the throttles: F7/F8 (Numpad 1/7) for engines 1–2, F9/F10 (Numpad 3/9) for 3–4, F5 together
More thrust on the left yaws and rolls you right — small, early inputs
Power up = nose up and climb, power down = descend; the aircraft oscillates (phugoid): lead it
Gravity gear early (O → Systems → ALT GEAR); a firm touchdown on the runway is a win

do.note: F/O: All three hydraulics — gone. I've got no controls! Nothing!
Captain: Throttles. We steer with the throttles.

objectives.text: Get it onto the runway — survivably
